Ama Owusu is a forty-eight-year-old train conductor with grey dreadlocks under a peaked cap, a burgundy uniform with gold buttons, and a silver ticket punch. Felix Brandt is a twenty-six-year-old violinist with a blond ponytail, a long camel coat and a battered violin case.

In the evening Ama blows her whistle on the platform. Felix runs along the train with his violin case. Ama punches Felix's ticket. Felix climbs aboard.

At night Felix orders soup in the dining car. Hana Sato, an eighty-year-old woman with a white bun, a lilac kimono jacket and a bamboo fan, sits down opposite him. Hana offers Felix a rice cracker. Felix tunes his violin. Felix plays a lullaby for Hana. Ama claps from the doorway.

Around midnight Ama checks the sleeper compartment. Hana searches her bag for her fan. Felix finds the fan under the bunk. Hana falls asleep.

At sunrise Ama opens the doors at the mountain station. Felix steps out into the snow. Hana waves her fan from the window. Ama hands Felix a forgotten scarf.

At noon Felix plays on a bench at the station for coins. Ama blows the whistle and the train leaves.
